UNIVERSAL.changelog:
Version 0.0.105 — the first update this board can actually find

Until now the device updater had nothing to check. It fetches a per-platform
manifest from the public distribution repo, but the release workflow only ever
attached a package to a GitHub release and never wrote that manifest, so every
update check failed. This release ships the missing publisher, and the manifest
now exists.

Integrity is checked against the manifest rather than against the package's own
metadata. A checksum stored inside an archive cannot attest to the archive that
contains it, which is why the in-package checksum field has always been empty
and the package's self-verification always passed. The manifest's SHA-256 lives
outside the artifact and is verified against the downloaded bytes before
anything is installed.

Also in this build:
- Streaming receive matches the ESP32 on every decode rule: preview-flagged
  E1.31 frames are never displayed, a terminating sender releases the outputs
  immediately, the DDP all-devices destination id is accepted, storage-flagged
  packets are not displayed, unsupported pixel formats are refused, and RGBW
  payloads pass through untouched so RGBW strips render correctly. The three
  protocol decoders are now literally the same code on both boards.
- DDP status and config queries are answered, so DDP-native discovery finds
  this board.
- Frame output waits for a complete frame instead of flipping mid-burst, so a
  slow multi-universe sender no longer shows half of one frame with half of the
  next.
- Pixel sources are arbitrated by priority rather than last-writer-wins: a
  running show is no longer stomped frame-by-frame by an effect or a sensor
  automation, and a source that stops writing stops owning the output.
- DMX channel mappings read from the correct source channels when universes are
  not 512 channels wide.
- Sunrise and sunset use the full NOAA solar algorithm, matching the ESP32
  minute for minute.
- Every thread the daemon runs now has a name, so `top -H` and crash reports
  are readable.
